terms.grammar: imperative of mittō, with or without an object (mitte istaec)
evidence: Ter. And. 762–764: Mitte id quod sciō

terms.gloss: don’t do over what’s done (let it go)

evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 132: missa faciam (Lewis & Short s.v. mittō)
terms.comment: “To treat as let go”: the neuter plural of missus with facere.

phrases.latin: Tacē: nōn fīet: mitte jam istaec: dā tē hodiē mihi: exporge frontem.
phrases.english: Hush, it won’t happen; drop all that; give me today; smooth your brow.
Don’t redo what’s done, as they say.
Drop it! No more of that!

sources: Lewis & Short: sino
